title: Groups facing difficulties in civil justice

draft.title: Groups facing difficulties in civil justice
card: Some groups can find civil justice hard to reach. Four are First Nations people, people on low incomes, young people, and people in rural and remote areas.
First Nations people and low incomes
First Nations people may face cultural barriers, distrust of the system and a lack of services that fit their needs. People on low incomes may not be able to pay for lawyers, fees or time off work.
Young people
Young people may not know their rights, and may find it hard to bring a claim without the help of an adult.
Rural and remote
People far from cities may have to travel long distances to reach courts, lawyers and other services.
draft.remember: Cost, culture, age and distance can each make civil justice hard to reach.

a.q: Which barrier is most likely to affect a person living in a remote town?
opts: Long travel to reach courts and lawyers
Not knowing their rights because of their age
Distrust of the system based on past experience
Being unable to pay for a lawyer
a.why: Distance means travel to reach courts and lawyers, which is the barrier the card links to rural and remote people. Age, cultural distrust and cost are linked to the other groups, though they can affect anyone.
a.clue: Think about where the remote town is, not who lives there.

b.q: Kai, aged 16, is owed wages by a café but does not know how to claim them. Which difficulty fits his situation best?
opts: Young people may not know their rights
Remote people must travel far to court
Low incomes mean legal fees are unaffordable
Cultural barriers make the system unfamiliar
b.why: Kai does not know how to claim, and his age is the reason given. Nothing says he lives far away, lacks money or faces cultural barriers. Cost is tempting, but the problem described is knowledge.
b.clue: What does Kai lack: money, distance or knowledge?

a.best: Long travel to reach courts and lawyers

b.best: Young people may not know their rights

problems.detail: The option 'Remote people must travel far to court' uses 'must', but the card says people far from cities 'may have to' travel long distances.

The right option is the only one hedged with 'may'. The distractors are absolute ('must travel', 'fees are unaffordable', 'make the system unfamiliar'), so a student could pick the hedged option without knowing the idea. 'Low incomes mean legal fees are unaffordable' also overstates the card's 'may not be able to pay'.
The why says 'his age is the reason given', but the question only states that Kai is 16. It never gives his age as the reason he does not know how to claim.

check.summary: The facts are sound and both intended answers are correct. In question b, the distractors use absolute wording ('must', 'unaffordable') while the right option alone says 'may', which gives the answer away. The why for b also claims the stem names age as the reason, which it does not.
